critical_evidence.evidence: The Carfax snapshot cites 6 service records and the listing states an August 2026 oil change. No invoices are shown, and there is no brake-fluid flush record, though one is due at about 3 years on a 2022 car.
The early-6MT failure risk applies to 2016 and early-2017 ND1 builds. This is a 2022 ND2 built after Mazda's internal revisions. Still ask for any warranty repair entries on the Carfax.
No photos with footwell carpet lifted or of the RF targa/rear drain areas. The seats and visible cabin look clean in the photos.

The Carfax shows at least one open recall, and the VIN lookup lists 24V695000 (airbag control module software). The seller cannot guarantee completion before close; the remedy is free at any Mazda dealer.
No tire DOT date photos and no battery date code or receipts. The tires are likely original 2022 Bridgestones, which is unverified.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are solid: VIN with matching decode, Carfax 1-owner/no-reported-accident snapshot, clean NJ title claim, $0 dealer fees, and underside photos plus a cold-start video. The maintenance half is incomplete: 6 Carfax service records are referenced but not shown, and there is no brake-fluid, tire-date or cabin-water evidence.

condition.rationale: The photos show a clean, dry, stock underside, a tidy unmodified engine bay, unworn leather and straight panels, consistent with 6k miles. There is no PPI and no scan. Age items (brake fluid, tires, battery) are unproven.

price_value.rationale: The $12,000 current bid is early and not meaningful. Comparable low-mile ND2 RF GTs sold at roughly $25k–$35k, so the likely hammer lands around the fair value estimate ($27.4k–$31.2k). The open recall is a free remedy.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual ND2 RF Grand Touring with very low miles, likely still within Mazda's powertrain warranty: reliable, rain-capable hardtop, easy to resell. Price will likely sit at the top of the budget band.

logistics.rationale: New Jersey to the Monterey Peninsula is a long transport, though BaT shipping is available. PPI access is not confirmed, but the dealer invites viewing contact. CA registration needs confirmation of a California emissions label because of the under-7,500-mile rule.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: The right model and a desirable spec (RF, Grand Touring, ND2 181 hp, manual, Bilsteins), but white paint is explicitly ruled out and the black interior is his least-preferred option. LSD/GT-S content is not established.

evidence.mission_note: A low-mile manual ND2 RF Grand Touring squarely matches the reliable, resellable enthusiast-bridge brief. The white-over-black colour combination conflicts with Jason's stated paint preference.
evidence.rationale: The VIN decode confirms a 2022 MX-5 RF Grand Touring with the 181 hp ND2 engine, and the photos confirm a manual gearbox, a stock engine bay and a clean, dry underside. The Carfax snapshot reports one owner, no accidents or damage, 6 service records and a last reading of 5,399 miles, which is consistent with the claimed 6k. One item is observed outright: an open airbag control module software recall (24V695000), whose remedy is free at a Mazda dealer. The flashing dash light was explained by the seller as LDWS switched off; that is unverified by a scan. Open items are the content of the service records (especially a brake-fluid flush due at about 3 years), tire and battery dates, RF seal and drain condition, LSD fitment, reserve status, and PPI access. California registration depends on an emissions label confirming CA conformity, because the car is under 7,500 miles. On spec it is a desirable ND2 RF, but the white exterior is on Jason's ruled-out list.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller today requesting a photo of the under-hood emissions label, the full Carfax service entries, and permission for a mobile PPI in Ramsey, NJ before the November 5 close.
